property_summary: After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs was zero, c.initialized() must be true and the contract balance unchanged by the call.
After seeding the market when marketDrugs is zero, c.initialized() must be true and the contract balance must remain equal to the balance before seeding.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is zero, c.initialized() must be true and the contract balance must remain equal to the balance before seeding.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is zero, initialized should be true and the contract balance should remain equal to the balance before seeding.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is initially zero, initialized must be true and the contract balance must remain equal to the balance before seeding.

For every admissible call to seedMarket, the reference contract sets initialized to true (so c.initialized() == true); the mutant leaves initialized false for some inputs, so the property fails there.

After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs was zero, getBalance() increases by the sent ETH (seedMarket is payable) while marketDrugs equals the provided drugs; in particular, address(c).balance >= msg_value passed to seedMarket.
After calling seedMarket with marketDrugs initially zero, the contract balance increases by at least the forwarded seedValue and marketDrugs equals the provided drugs.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is initially zero, the contract balance increases by at least the forwarded seedValue and marketDrugs equals the provided drugs.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is zero, the contract balance increases by at least the forwarded seedValue and marketDrugs equals the provided drugs.
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is initially zero, the contract balance should increase by at least the forwarded seedValue and marketDrugs should equal the provided drugs.

For any caller and any initial drugs>0, calling seedMarket on the correct contract sets initialized to true (and marketDrugs to the supplied amount) while the mutant that omits setting initialized can leave initialized false for some inputs; thus initialized==true after seedMarket is a universal property of the reference and is violated by the mutant for some inputs.
After calling seedMarket(drugs) with any drugs value, c.initialized() must be true iff c.marketDrugs() != 0 (i.e., initialized becomes true whenever marketDrugs is nonzero).
After seeding when marketDrugs equals 0 prior to the call, c.initialized becomes true regardless of the input drugs value (i.e., seedMarket always sets initialized=true when it is the first seed).
After seeding the market from zero, initialized remains true and the contract reports initialized == true (so seedMarket cannot leave initialized false).
After calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is initially zero, the contract becomes initialized (initialized == true).

Calling seedMarket when marketDrugs is zero makes the contract report initialized == true afterwards (so address(c).balance and marketDrugs reflect a seeded market only when initialized is set), i.e., marketDrugs > 0 implies initialized is true after seeding from zero.

If marketDrugs is zero before seedMarket is called, then after calling seedMarket(payable) the contract's marketDrugs equals the supplied drugs argument (i.e., seedMarket sets marketDrugs to the parameter when initially zero).
If marketDrugs is zero before calling seedMarket, then after calling seedMarket(drugs) the contract's marketDrugs equals the supplied drugs argument.

For any caller, calling DrugDealer() on the reference contract always leaves initialized unchanged (remains false since only ceoAddress can call and DrugDealer sets ceoAddress = msg.sender without touching initialized), but the mutant toggles initialized when seedMarket is called so there exists a sequence (seedMarket then DrugDealer) where initialized differs — we assert that calling DrugDealer() does not change initialized in the reference (so initialized before == after).

For any caller and any prior state, calling DrugDealer() does not change the contract's initialized flag on the correct contract (initialized_after == initialized_before); the mutant flips initialized when seedMarket is called which can make initialized differ after operations, so the property detects that difference.

For the correct contract, calling seedMarket(uint256) when marketDrugs==0 always sets initialized to true; the mutant that toggles initialized can leave initialized false for some fuzzed drugs value, so the property is: after seedMarket on a fresh contract, initialized == true (holds for reference, violated by mutant for some inputs).

For any caller and any nonzero payable seed amount, after calling seedMarket(uint256) on a fresh-deployed contract (marketDrugs==0) the reference always sets initialized to true and the mutant that toggles initialized can leave initialized false for some fuzzed ether amounts; we assert initialized==true after seedMarket when the call is made with any nonzero msg.value and marketDrugs==0.

For any caller and any drugs value when marketDrugs==0, calling seedMarket(drugs) then immediately calling the public getter initialized() returns true on the reference contract (seedMarket always sets initialized=true), whereas the mutant that toggles initialized can leave initialized false for some fuzzed drugs input and msg.value combination.

After seeding a zero market, the contract becomes initialized before its marketDrugs getter reflects the seeded nonzero value (i.e., initialized is true only if marketDrugs was nonzero at the moment of initialization).

Calling seedMarket on a fresh contract (marketDrugs == 0) always reverts when msg.sender is not the contract itself (i.e., external caller cannot seed market), so seedMarket should revert for any caller address other than the contract.
external call to seedMarket must revert (original contract enforces a condition that causes revert here)
Calling seedMarket(1) from this test contract with zero value must revert (reverted == true).
The call to c.seedMarket{value: 0}(1) must revert (reverted == true).

After seeding the market with seedMarket, calling DrugDealer (which sets ceoAddress only if msg.sender==ceoAddress) must leave initialized unchanged (true) for the correct contract for all inputs; the mutant that sets initialized after marketDrugs assignment can cause initialized to be false after the same sequence when seedMarket's ordering interacts with msg.sender checks (the test fuzzes the initial ether and caller to trigger the difference).

For any caller and any seed amount/ether, after calling seedMarket(...) the contract's initialized() becomes true immediately (i.e., seedMarket always sets initialized true regardless of msg.sender/calls), whereas the mutant that moves initialized assignment below marketDrugs assignment can be observed to leave initialized false for some reentrant/failing external caller behavior when seedMarket's external transfer (to ceoAddress in other flows) interacts — we will trigger difference by having seedMarket be called re-entering via a attacker that reverts in its fallback so ordering matters (the correct contract sets initialized to true in all cases but the mutant can be observed false).

After any call to seedMarket(...) completes (for any fuzzed initial ether value and any fuzzed caller used to fund the contract), the reference sets initialized == true unconditionally, whereas the mutant's reordering can leave initialized == false when a malicious/failing external recipient causes an interaction ordering difference.

For any caller address and any ether value used to seed the contract, if seedMarket(drugs) is called (succeeds) before calling DrugDealer(), then calling DrugDealer() by the current ceoAddress must leave initialized == true in the reference but the mutant (which sets initialized after marketDrugs assignment) can produce initialized == false for some fuzzed inputs when reentrancy/failing external behavior interacts with sequencing — we detect this by fuzzing the seed amount and the attacker address that will be used as ceo and may revert on calls, asserting initialized is true after DrugDealer() returns.

For every caller and ether amount used to seed the market and for any adversarial ceo-like address that reverts when receiving Ether, calling seedMarket(...) followed by DrugDealer() always leaves initialized == true in the reference contract, but the mutant (which sets initialized after assigning marketDrugs) can observe initialized == false for some fuzzed inputs when the ceoAddress's fallback reverts while seedMarket is executing.
Only the original CEO can set ceoAddress via DrugDealer(); after a call by non-CEO, the contract's ceoAddress remains the original CEO.

property_summary: Only the current CEO (the address returned by ceoAddress()) can successfully call DrugDealer(); any caller address different from that must cause DrugDealer() to revert.
Only the contract's current CEO address can successfully call DrugDealer(); calls from any other address must revert.
Calls to DrugDealer() revert unless msg.sender equals the contract's current ceoAddress.
Invoking DrugDealer() must revert for any caller that is not already the contract's current ceoAddress.

For all callers, calling DrugDealer() on the reference contract only succeeds (or only the CEO can set ceoAddress) when invoked by the existing ceoAddress (i.e., ceoAddress remains unchanged unless called by the current CEO); the mutant allows any caller to change ceoAddress to themselves, which violates this invariant for some caller addresses.
After calling DrugDealer(), the ceoAddress remains equal to the caller (msg.sender) — i.e., the contract accepts a call that sets ceoAddress to the caller.
